question: Under a true null, does repeated uncorrected A/B significance testing inflate false positives?
significance: Experiment design requires valid false-discovery controls when teams repeatedly inspect outcomes.
hypothesis: Five uncorrected interim z-tests at 5% nominal alpha exceed the fixed-final-test false positive rate, while Bonferroni controls family-wise error.
falsifier: Uncorrected any-look false-positive rate is no higher than fixed-final rate, or adjusted rate exceeds nominal level by practically meaningful margin.
